docs.title: Data Transfer
docs.text: This page answers common operational and technical questions regarding data ingress and file transfers into the GlasgowTRE environment.

docs.title: 1. Is this an HTTPS transfer service, or an HTTP wrapper for an SFTP one?
docs.text:
It is neither an HTTP wrapper nor a proxy.

The service runs a unified, native multi-protocol transfer engine (SFTPGo) supporting both:

  • HTTPS (web-transfer interface via port 443)
  • Native SFTP (via port 2022)

Both protocols connect directly to the same underlying storage and authentication service. Files uploaded through either protocol arrive in the same target directories with identical permissions and access controls.

docs.title: 2. Is the service suitable for multiple 500GB individual files (e.g. 23 files totaling ~11.5 TB in one operation)?
docs.text:
The recommended protocol depends heavily on the volume and individual file sizes:

  • SFTP (Port 2022 — Strongly Recommended): Yes. A dedicated SFTP client (such as Cyberduck, FileZilla, WinSCP, or CLI tools like sftp / rsync over SSH) can queue all 23 files (~11.5 TB total) in a single operation and process the queue automatically without manual intervention.
  • HTTPS (Web Transfer — Not Recommended for Large Files): While the web interface technically allows queuing multiple files, uploading individual 500GB files via a web browser is very prone to browser tab crashes, memory exhaustion, and HTTP proxy or network timeouts.

Browser Upload Limitations

For datasets with individual files larger than a few gigabytes, or total batch sizes in the hundreds of gigabytes or terabytes, always use native SFTP (Port 2022) rather than the web browser interface.

docs.title: 3. Will it process multiple files in parallel or sequentially?
docs.text:
• HTTPS (Web Transfer): Sequentially only. The web interface transfers 1 file at a time; it only triggers the next upload once the current file completes.
  • SFTP (Port 2022): While the SFTP protocol inherently supports multiple concurrent connections, we advise against configuring parallel transfers at this time. Because the GlasgowTRE service enforces Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), each new concurrent connection spawned by an SFTP client triggers a separate 2FA prompt/challenge. This can lead to session disruptions, timeout errors, and failed parallel streams.

Client Setting Recommendation: Limit to 1 Transfer at a Time

We strongly recommend configuring your SFTP client queue settings to 1 transfer at a time (sequential).

Roadmap: Parallel Transfers

We recognise the importance of parallel transfers for high-volume data and are actively investigating secure mechanisms to enable concurrent streams without repeated MFA prompts in the future.

docs.title: 4. Does the service support resuming paused or interrupted uploads?
docs.text:
• HTTPS (Web Transfer): No. The web browser client does not support resumable or chunked uploads. If a browser upload is interrupted or the network drops, the transfer must restart from 0%.
  • SFTP (Port 2022): Yes. Native SFTP clients support resuming/appending to interrupted or paused uploads based on byte offsets. Given 500GB file sizes, resumability is essential to prevent restarting multi-hour transfers from scratch in the event of transient network disruptions or client disconnections.

docs.title: 5. How can I verify that large transfers arrived without corruption?
docs.text:
Before transferring your dataset, generate a cryptographic checksum manifest (e.g. SHA256SUMS). Once the upload completes, run the verification command on the destination GlasgowTRE workstation to confirm byte-for-byte integrity.

For complete step-by-step instructions and commands across Linux and Windows, see our guide on How to prepare a data transfer manifest and the Preparing Data for Transfer FAQ.

docs.title: Preparing Data for Transfer
docs.text: This page answers frequently asked questions regarding data preparation, checksum manifest standards, and payload verification for uploads to GlasgowTRE.

docs.title: 1. Do I need to create a checksum manifest before transferring data?
docs.text: Yes. We strongly recommend generating a checksum manifest for every dataset uploaded to GlasgowTRE. Transferring multi-gigabyte or terabyte datasets across networks can occasionally result in subtle corruption, truncated files, or network dropouts. Having a pre-computed manifest allows you and the GlasgowTRE system to cryptographically verify bit-for-bit file integrity after arrival.

docs.title: 2. Which checksum format and algorithm should I use?
docs.text:
GlasgowTRE recommends the industry-standard GNU Coreutils SHA-256 format:

  • Filename: SHA256SUMS
  • Format: <sha256-hex> <filename> (two spaces between the 64-character lowercase hexadecimal hash and the filename)
  • Algorithm: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4, collision-resistant)

This standard format is natively verified on Linux systems via sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS and easily validated across Windows and macOS environments.

docs.title: 3. Can I use MD5 or a tab-separated manifest instead?
docs.text:
While some legacy workflows use MD5 or custom formats like <filename><TAB><md5>, this architecture is not recommended for modern research data governance:

  1. Cryptographic Weakness: MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks (RFC 6151). While sufficient for accidental bit flips, it fails institutional data security baselines.
  2. Tool Incompatibility: Inverting columns breaks native check flags (sha256sum -c or md5sum -c), requiring recipients to write custom parsing scripts.

docs.title: 4. How do I avoid cross-platform encoding and line-ending issues between Windows and Linux?
docs.text:
When generating checksum manifests on Windows to be verified on Linux:

  • Avoid UTF-8 Byte Order Marks (BOM): Standard Linux utilities (sha256sum) interpret the 3-byte UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) as part of the first filename or hash, triggering parsing errors. Always emit UTF-8 without BOM (e.g. using [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) in PowerShell).
  • Line Endings: While GNU coreutils 8.27+ handles Windows CRLF (\r\n) gracefully in standard formats, custom parsers often break. Using POSIX LF (\n) is safest across all platforms.
  • Paths and Directory Separators: Use relative filenames or paths (e.g. file.dat or subfolder/file.dat) with forward slashes (/) rather than Windows backslashes (\), and avoid absolute Windows drive paths (C:\...). Linux utilities interpret backslashes as literal filename characters rather than directory separators.

docs.title: 5. Where can I find the step-by-step commands to generate and verify manifests?
docs.text:
For complete step-by-step instructions with command tabs for Linux (Bash), Windows (PowerShell), and Windows (Command Prompt), see our dedicated guide:

👉 How to prepare a data transfer manifest

docs.title: 6. What other steps should I take before transferring large datasets?
docs.text:
• Consolidate small files: If transferring millions of small files, consider archiving them into .tar or compressed archives first to prevent file system metadata bottlenecks.
  • Check transfer protocol: For datasets exceeding a few gigabytes, use native SFTP (Port 2022) rather than the web browser interface. See the Data Transfer FAQ for details on resumable transfers and connection parameters.

docs.title: [DRAFT] How to connect to GlasgowTRE secure VPN and workstation
Objective
docs.text: Use this guide to configure and establish a secure FortiClient VPN connection to GlasgowTRE, authenticate using two-factor authentication (2FA), access your remote TRE research workstation, and sign out securely at the end of your session.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  • A University-owned, managed device with up-to-date operating system patches and active antivirus software.
  • Administrative privileges on your device (or assistance from your local IT support team) to install software.
  • Your KeePass database archive (KeePass-2.61.1.zip or similar) received via the University of Glasgow transfer system.
  • Your master KeePass password delivered via Microsoft Teams.
  • Your assigned GlasgowTRE username (formatted as xxx.xxx.xxx@glasgowtre.ac.uk) received via email from the TRE support team.
  • The FortiClientVPNInstaller.exe installer file downloaded from the link provided in your onboarding materials.
  • Access to your registered email inbox to receive time-sensitive two-factor authentication codes.
  • A stable internet connection on a trusted network (such as the campus network, home broadband, or approved corporate connection).

Security Requirement: Managed Devices Only

Access to the Glasgow Trusted Research Environment is strictly restricted to University-owned and centrally managed devices. The use of personal computers, unmanaged laptops, tablets, or mobile phones is strictly prohibited. Any connection attempt originating from an unmanaged device will fail network compliance checks and be blocked.

Distinct TRE Credentials

Your GlasgowTRE credentials are dedicated to your specific research project and are completely separate from your standard University of Glasgow GUID and email credentials. Never attempt to log in using standard university single sign-on credentials, and never share your TRE login details.

docs.title: Step 1: Retrieve your login password from KeePass
docs.text:
Your GlasgowTRE passwords are transmitted inside an encrypted KeePass database file to prevent unauthorised exposure.

  1. Locate and extract the KeePass database package (KeePass-2.61.1.zip) received via the UofG file transfer service.
  2. Launch KeePass.exe.
  3. Open your project database file and enter the master password sent to you via Microsoft Teams when prompted.
  4. Locate the entries for your GlasgowTRE VPN and GlasgowTRE Workstation accounts.
  5. Copy or record your unique password. Note that your assigned TRE username (received via your onboarding email) remains constant across both services.

docs.title: Step 2: Download and install FortiClient VPN
docs.text:
All network communication with the GlasgowTRE infrastructure must travel through an encrypted FortiClient SSL-VPN tunnel.

  1. Download the authorised installer file FortiClientVPNInstaller.exe from the onboarding link provided by the TRE support team.
  2. Run the installer and proceed through the setup wizard using the default installation settings.
  3. Open the FortiClient application once installation finishes.
  4. Select the menu icon (three horizontal lines) in the upper-right corner of the interface and select Add a new connection.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure the VPN connection profile
docs.text:
Configure a dedicated VPN profile for the GlasgowTRE secure gateway.

  1. In the New Connection dialogue, select SSL-VPN.
  2. Enter the connection parameters as specified in the table below:
Setting Value VPN SSL-VPN Connection Name GlasgowTRE Description Glasgow TRE Secure Access Remote Gateway vpn.glasgowtre.ac.uk Customize port Checked (leave default 443 or as configured) Enable Single Sign On (SSO) for VPN Tunnel Unchecked Client Certificate None Authentication Select Save Login Username Enter your full TRE username (e.g. xxx.xxx.xxx@glasgowtre.ac.uk)
  1. Confirm that the configuration matches the expected gateway details before saving.

  1. Select Save to store the connection profile.

docs.title: Step 4: Connect to the VPN with Two-Factor Authentication
docs.text:
Every VPN session requires multi-factor authentication using a dynamic verification code delivered to your registered email address.

  1. On the FortiClient home screen, select the GlasgowTRE profile from the VPN Name dropdown.
  2. Confirm your TRE username is entered correctly.
  3. Enter your TRE password retrieved from KeePass into the Password field.
  4. Select Connect.

  1. When primary credentials are accepted, FortiClient will display a prompt requesting an authentication Token.

  1. Open your registered email inbox and check for a message containing your six-digit authentication code. This email is sent automatically when the token prompt appears.

Enter the Token Promptly

The six-digit email token is time-limited. Enter the token into FortiClient immediately upon receipt. If the token expires or is rejected, restart the connection attempt from the FortiClient login screen to request a fresh token.

  1. Return to FortiClient, type the six-digit code into the Token field, and select OK.

  1. Wait for the connection progress to complete. Once established, the FortiClient dashboard displays a green checkmark, your assigned TRE internal IP address, connection duration, and an active Disconnect button.

docs.title: Step 5: Download the Secure Workstation Access package
docs.text:
With the VPN connection established, download the dedicated workstation access package to reach your allocated virtual environment.

  1. Ensure your FortiClient VPN is active and connected.
  2. Navigate to the Secure Workstation Access download link provided in your onboarding email.
  3. If prompted with a browser confirmation to connect to the service, confirm and proceed.

  1. If your web browser flags the download with a security warning stating that the file is not commonly downloaded or has an unknown publisher:
  2. Select the options menu (...) or review panel next to the download item.
  3. Choose Keep (or Keep anyway).

  1. Open your local Downloads folder and confirm that the workstation executable package is present.

docs.title: Step 6: Connect to the TRE workstation via Remote Desktop
docs.text:
Launch the workstation connection package to open an encrypted Remote Desktop session into the TRE.

  1. Double-click the downloaded workstation executable package in your Downloads folder.
  2. When the Remote Desktop Connection security dialogue appears with the notice "The publisher of this remote connection cannot be identified. Do you want to connect anyway?", select Connect.

  1. On the Windows Security - RD Gateway Security Credentials prompt, select Use a different account.

  1. Enter your full GlasgowTRE credentials:
  2. User name: Enter your complete TRE username in the format xxx.xxx.xxx@glasgowtre.ac.uk.
  3. Password: Enter your TRE password retrieved from KeePass in Step 1.
  4. Select OK.

  1. When the certificate verification prompt appears stating "The identity of the remote computer cannot be verified. Do you want to connect anyway?", select Yes to trust the connection.

  1. The GlasgowTRE workstation desktop will launch in full screen. You are now inside your secure research environment and can access your approved datasets and analytics tools.

docs.title: Step 7: Sign out securely and disconnect the VPN
docs.text:
Always perform a full sign out from the workstation before disconnecting from the network. Simply closing the remote desktop window leaves active sessions and locks workstation resources.

  1. Inside the remote TRE workstation, click the Start button on the Windows taskbar (or press the Windows key).
  2. Select your User Profile icon at the top or side of the Start menu.
  3. Select Sign out.

  1. Wait for the remote desktop session window to close cleanly.
  2. On your local device, open the FortiClient window.
  3. Select Disconnect to terminate the encrypted VPN tunnel.

docs.title: If you need help
docs.text: If you experience connection errors, need password resets, or encounter issues with two-factor authentication, contact the GlasgowTRE support team.

docs.title: Primary support channel: UofG Helpdesk Portal
docs.text:
Log a support ticket through the central University of Glasgow Helpdesk service catalogue:

  1. Navigate to the UofG Helpdesk Portal.
  2. Select Service Catalogue.
  3. Select Report Something.
  4. Choose Glasgow TRE Helpdesk and Technical Support.

  1. Complete the support form with the following details:
  2. Step affected: Specify the exact step number and process (e.g. FortiClient installation, 2FA code, RD Gateway login).
  3. Error details: Include exact error messages, error codes, or screenshots of the failure.
  4. Timestamp: Note the approximate date and time the incident occurred.
  5. TRE Username: Provide your TRE username (e.g. xxx.xxx.xxx@glasgowtre.ac.uk).

Do Not Share Passwords in Tickets

Never include your KeePass master password, TRE login password, or two-factor authentication codes in support tickets or email correspondence.

docs.title: Urgent support and direct email contact
docs.text:
If the Helpdesk portal is unavailable, or if you are facing a critical project deadline, contact the TRE Support Team directly by email:

  • Email: tre@glasgow.ac.uk

docs.title: How to use GlasgowTRE secure web file transfer service
Objective
docs.text: Use this guide to sign in to the Glasgow TRE secure transfer service, complete first-time two-factor authentication setup, and begin managing files.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  • Your username from the welcome email.
  • Your password from the separate communication channel.
  • A mobile device with an authenticator app such as Microsoft Authenticator.
  • A working internet connection and access to the service URL.

Self-service password changes are not available. If you forget your password or cannot sign in, contact the helpdesk instead of trying to bypass the security process.

docs.title: Step 1: Open the service
docs.text:
1. Open the service URL: http://sftp.glasgowtre.ac.uk/
  2. Enter your username and password.
  3. Select Sign In.
  4. TEST TEST TEST

docs.title: Step 2: Complete first-time two-factor authentication setup
docs.text:
On your first successful sign in, you will be asked to configure two-factor authentication.

  1. Open the Configuration section.
  2. In the service dropdown, choose GlasgowTRE (DataTransfer Service).
  3. In the Require 2FA dropdown, choose HTTP.
  4. Select Enable.

  1. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app.
  2. If the QR code cannot be scanned, use the manual entry option instead:
  3. Open the authenticator app.
  4. Choose Add account.
  5. Select Enter code manually.
  6. Choose Other (Google, Facebook, etc.)
  7. Enter an account name such as Glasgow TRE and the secret key shown on screen.

  1. Enter the current six-digit code from the authenticator app into the Authentication Code field immediately.

Codes are time-based and expire every 30 seconds, so enter the latest code as soon as it appears.

docs.title: Step 3: Sign in on later sessions
docs.text:
For future visits:

  1. Return to the same service URL.
  2. Enter your username and password.
  3. Enter the six-digit code from the GlasgowTRE (DataTransfer Service) entry in your authenticator app.
  4. Confirm that you reach the Files view.

docs.title: Step 4: Upload and manage files
docs.text:
Once you are signed in:

  1. Open the Files section.
  2. Create a new folder if needed by selecting New Folder and giving it a name.

  1. Upload files by dragging them into the upload area or using Browse folder.
  2. Use Preview, Rename, Move, Copy, or Delete as needed.

Planning large or bulk file transfers (500GB+)?

Uploading large datasets through a web browser is prone to tab crashes and network timeouts, and cannot be resumed if interrupted. For high-volume data transfers, we strongly recommend using native SFTP (Port 2022). See our Data Transfer FAQ for architecture details, concurrency limits, and recommended client settings. Before transferring, generate an integrity manifest by following our How to prepare a data transfer manifest guide.

docs.title: Step 5: End the session securely
docs.text:
1. Select the profile icon in the top-right corner.
  2. Choose Sign Out.
  3. Confirm that you are returned to the sign-in screen.

docs.title: If you need help
docs.text: If you are unable to sign in, cannot use the authenticator app, or need a password reset, contact the UofG Helpdesk through the service catalogue and select the Data (incl. Data ingress/extraction) category. You can also contact the team directly at tre@glasgow.ac.uk.

docs.title: Quick Reference: Recommended SFTP Client Configuration
docs.text:
When setting up your transfer client (Cyberduck, WinSCP, FileZilla, etc.) for large ingest workloads:

Setting Recommended Value Rationale Protocol SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) Direct protocol engine, supports byte-offset resuming. Port 2022 Dedicated native SFTP listener. Maximum Concurrent Connections 1 Avoids triggering multiple concurrent 2FA challenges. Transfer Mode / Queue Sequential (1 file at a time) Ensures reliable batch processing through large queues. Existing Files / Interrupted Action Resume (or Append) Prevents restarting 500GB+ files from 0% on disconnect.

docs.title: How to prepare a data transfer manifest
Objective
docs.text: Generate a checksum manifest for your dataset before uploading to GlasgowTRE, and verify file integrity upon arrival to guarantee that no files were corrupted, truncated, or modified during transit.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  • A local directory containing the files you intend to transfer.
  • Terminal access on your operating system:
    • Linux / macOS: Bash or Zsh with standard core utilities (sha256sum, find, sort).
    • Windows: PowerShell 5.1 / PowerShell 7+ or Command Prompt (cmd.exe).
  • Read permissions on all data files and write permissions to create the manifest file.

docs.title: Step 1: Open a terminal in the target data directory
docs.text:
Navigate to the directory containing your payload files:

Linux (Bash)Windows (PowerShell)Windows (Command Prompt) 
cd /path/to/data-folder

Set-Location "C:\path\to\data-folder"

cd /d "C:\path\to\data-folder"

docs.title: Step 2: Generate the manifest (Recommended: SHA-256)
docs.text:
The standard GlasgowTRE format follows the GNU Coreutils checksum standard (<hash> <filename>) using SHA-256. The output file is named SHA256SUMS.

Run the appropriate command for your operating system:

Linux (Bash)Windows (PowerShell)Windows (Command Prompt) 
find . -type f ! -name "SHA256SUMS" -exec sha256sum {} + \
  | sed 's|  \./|  |' \
  | sort -k2 > SHA256SUMS

Flat and nested directory support

The find command above recursively discovers files across all subfolders, normalizes relative paths (subfolder/file.ext), and safely excludes the manifest itself. It works identically for flat directories containing only root-level files.

[System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines(
    "$PWD\SHA256SUMS",
    [string[]]@(
        Get-ChildItem -File -Recurse |
            Where-Object Name -ne 'SHA256SUMS' |
            Sort-Object FullName |
            ForEach-Object {
                $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
                $relPath = $_.FullName.Substring($PWD.Path.Length).TrimStart('\').Replace('\', '/')
                "$hash  $relPath"
            }
    ),
    [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)
)

UTF-8 without BOM, POSIX path separators, and literal paths

Using [System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines with [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) prevents Windows PowerShell 5.1 from injecting a Byte Order Mark (BOM). Normalizing directory separators with .Replace('\', '/') produces POSIX-standard relative paths (subfolder/file.ext) required by Linux sha256sum -c. Passing -LiteralPath ensures filenames or directories containing brackets ([ and ]) are hashed accurately without wildcard interpretation errors.

powershell -NoProfile -Command ^
  "[System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines('SHA256SUMS', " ^
  "[string[]]@(Get-ChildItem -File -Recurse | " ^
  "Where-Object Name -ne 'SHA256SUMS' | " ^
  "Sort-Object FullName | " ^
  "ForEach-Object { " ^
  "  $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower(); " ^
  "  $rel = $_.FullName.Substring($PWD.Path.Length).TrimStart('\').Replace('\', '/'); " ^
  "  ($hash + '  ' + $rel) " ^
  "}), " ^
  "[System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))"

Nested subdirectories and archiving

All commands above recursively process files across all nested subdirectories out of the box, preserving relative folder paths. If your dataset contains tens of thousands of small files, archiving them into a single compressed archive before transfer is still recommended for transfer performance (see FAQ Question 6).

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the manifest locally before transfer
docs.text:
Verify the manifest against your local files before uploading to confirm the checksums were recorded accurately.

Linux (Bash)Windows (PowerShell)Windows (Command Prompt) 
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

Get-Content SHA256SUMS |
    Where-Object { $_ -match '\S' } |
    ForEach-Object {
        $expectedHash, $file = $_ -split '\s+', 2
        $valid = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) -and
            ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -eq $expectedHash.ToLower())
        $status = if ($valid) { "OK" } else { "FAILED" }
        [PSCustomObject]@{ File = $file; Status = $status }
    }

powershell -NoProfile -Command ^
  "Get-Content SHA256SUMS | " ^
  "Where-Object { $_ -match '\S' } | " ^
  "ForEach-Object { " ^
  "  $expectedHash, $file = $_ -split '\s+', 2; " ^
  "  $valid = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) -and " ^
  "    ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -eq $expectedHash.ToLower()); " ^
  "  $status = if ($valid) { 'OK' } else { 'FAILED' }; " ^
  "  [PSCustomObject]@{ File = $file; Status = $status } " ^
  "}"

docs.title: Verification checkpoint
docs.text:
Every file must report OK:

Linux (Bash)Windows (PowerShell)Windows (Command Prompt) 
dataset_part1.tar.gz: OK
metadata.csv: OK
raw_data/sample_01.fastq: OK
raw_data/sample_02.fastq: OK

File                     Status
----                     ------
dataset_part1.tar.gz     OK    
metadata.csv             OK    
raw_data/sample_01.fastq OK    
raw_data/sample_02.fastq OK    

File                     Status
----                     ------
dataset_part1.tar.gz     OK    
metadata.csv             OK    
raw_data/sample_01.fastq OK    
raw_data/sample_02.fastq OK

If any file displays FAILED or MISSING, investigate whether the file was modified, in use, or locked before proceeding.

docs.title: Step 4: Transfer files and manifest to GlasgowTRE
docs.text:
1. Upload your data files alongside the generated SHA256SUMS file into your GlasgowTRE target folder using SFTP (Port 2022) or the web transfer service.
  2. Ensure SHA256SUMS sits in the exact same directory as the payload files it describes.

See How to use GlasgowTRE secure web file transfer service for transfer service login instructions.

docs.title: Step 5: Verify file integrity after transfer
docs.text:
Once the upload completes, or once you sign in to your GlasgowTRE workstation, verify that the files arrived intact without bit rot or packet corruption.

Run the verification command inside the destination directory:

Linux (Bash)Windows (PowerShell)Windows (Command Prompt) 
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

To suppress noise and only print files that fail: 

sha256sum --quiet -c SHA256SUMS


Get-Content SHA256SUMS |
    Where-Object { $_ -match '\S' } |
    ForEach-Object {
        $expectedHash, $file = $_ -split '\s+', 2
        $valid = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) -and
            ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -eq $expectedHash.ToLower())
        $status = if ($valid) { "OK" } else { "FAILED" }
        [PSCustomObject]@{ File = $file; Status = $status }
    }

powershell -NoProfile -Command ^
  "Get-Content SHA256SUMS | " ^
  "Where-Object { $_ -match '\S' } | " ^
  "ForEach-Object { " ^
  "  $expectedHash, $file = $_ -split '\s+', 2; " ^
  "  $valid = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) -and " ^
  "    ((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -eq $expectedHash.ToLower()); " ^
  "  $status = if ($valid) { 'OK' } else { 'FAILED' }; " ^
  "  [PSCustomObject]@{ File = $file; Status = $status } " ^
  "}"

docs.title: Verification checkpoint
docs.text:
• A return code of 0 and OK on all items confirms complete cryptographic integrity.
  • If any file fails verification, re-transfer that specific file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Root Cause Resolution No such file or directory during -c verification The manifest file was run from a different directory than where the files reside. Run the verification command directly within the folder containing both the manifest and data files. Verification fails on the first file on Linux (: no such file) The manifest was generated on Windows with a UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF). Re-generate using the provided PowerShell snippet which explicitly enforces [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false). Linux verification fails with No such file or directory on nested files (\subdir\file: FAILED open or read) The manifest was generated on Windows with backslashes (\) instead of POSIX slashes (/). Re-generate using the provided PowerShell snippet (which converts paths with .Replace('\', '/')), or convert existing separators on Linux via tr '\\' '/' < SHA256SUMS \| sha256sum -c. PowerShell throws InvokeMethodOnNull or generates empty hashes on paths with [ or ] Get-FileHash treats square brackets as wildcard pattern boundaries when -LiteralPath is omitted. Re-generate using the provided snippets which specify -LiteralPath for all hashing and path validation calls. Linux md5sum -c fails with no properly formatted checksum lines found on manifest.txt The manifest contains Windows CRLF line endings (\r\n) that append \r to the hash field. Run the verification command which uses sub(/\r$/, "", $2) in awk to strip carriage returns before piping to md5sum -c. FAILED checksum on large files The upload was interrupted, truncated, or suffered network corruption. Re-transfer the affected file via SFTP (port 2022) with resume capability enabled. Subdirectories reported as directories during hash generation Using wildcards like sha256sum * attempts to pass directories directly to the hashing binary. Use the recommended find . -type f command which filters exclusively for files and traverses nested directories.

docs.text: This document establishes the architecture and content design for introducing the Software section into the Glasgow TRE Handbook website (glasgowtre.github.io). docs.title: 3.1 Toolchain & Architecture
docs.text:
• Tool: Astral uv deployed system-wide (C:\Program Files\uv on Windows analytics workstations).
  • Security & Privileges: All Python environment management, runtime switching, and dependency installations take place in user space without requiring local administrator rights.
  • Python Binary Distribution:
  • Python binaries are sourced upstream from astral-sh/python-build-standalone.
  • Version coverage includes all releases from 3.12.0 to 3.14.13 (including beta and RC builds).
  • Supported platforms: Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) and Linux (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu).
  • Binaries are mirrored internally to internal HTTP/PowerScale S3 object storage (python-install-mirror).
  • Enforcement:
  • C:\ProgramData\uv\uv.toml sets python-preference = "only-managed" to ensure workstations strictly pull and run mirrored runtimes.
  • Package Repository (PyPI Mirror):
  • Glasgow TRE hosts an internal air-gapped Pulp mirror serving curated wheels and source distributions (repo.hlz.glasgowtre.ac.uk).
  • Pre-configured C:\ProgramData\pip\pip.ini (Windows) and /etc/pip.conf (Linux) allow standard pip and Jupyter %pip commands to resolve dependencies automatically.

docs.title: 1. Header & Overview
docs.text:
• Title: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
  • Our Approach: Glasgow TRE provides native Linux capability within Windows workstations. Rather than forcing a pre-installed instance on all workstations, the platform provisions access to an approved enterprise Linux distribution.
  • Distribution: Pre-configured Rocky Linux 10 WSL distribution tailored for scientific computing and TRE compliance.
  • Enterprise Provisioning: WSL features and distro access are pre-configured through Glasgow TRE automated workstation management (glasgowtre-ansible).

docs.title: 3. File System Access & Interoperability
docs.text:
• Navigating Windows project shares from WSL:
  • Windows drives mounted under /mnt/c/, /mnt/v/ (project data share).
  • Best practice tips:
  • Keep high-performance I/O and compiled code inside the Linux filesystem (/home/<user>/...) or map to /mnt/v/ for persistent shared artifacts.
  • Accessing WSL files from Windows Explorer via \\wsl$\rocky-10\.

docs.title: 1. Header & Overview
docs.text:
• Title: Containers & Apptainer
  • No Third-Party Desktop Runtimes: Glasgow TRE enables native container execution inside WSL without requiring heavy third-party desktop utilities (such as Docker Desktop or Podman Desktop), avoiding licensing, elevated privilege, and background service overhead.
  • Primary Scientific Runtime: Apptainer (formerly Singularity) is provided as the primary container system for reproducible research, batch computing, and HPC parity.
  • OCI Container Support: Lightweight rootless container tools available natively within the Rocky Linux 10 WSL environment.

docs.title: 2. Why Apptainer for Glasgow TRE?
docs.text:
• Unprivileged user execution (no root daemon or elevated rights required).
  • Single-file container image format (.sif), making experiments easily portable, versionable, and auditable.
  • Native access to host GPUs and filesystem paths without complex network virtualization.

docs.title: 3. Quick Start & Common Workflows
docs.text:
• Running an Apptainer Container: 
    apptainer run my_analysis.sif
  • Interactive Shell inside a Container: 
    apptainer shell --bind /mnt/v/project:/data my_analysis.sif
  • Executing a Specific Command: 
    apptainer exec my_analysis.sif python script.py
  • Building / Converting Images:
  • Converting OCI/Docker archive images to SIF format or building from definition files within the enclave.

docs.title: 4. Rootless OCI Container Workflows
docs.text:
• Running standard OCI containers within WSL using native rootless tools (e.g. podman inside the Rocky 10 WSL instance).
  • Comparison table: When to choose Apptainer (scientific workloads, pipelines, HPC parity) vs. OCI containers (microservices, web servers, developer tools).

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
You can use LibreOffice in the Glasgow TRE to open and check CSV and Excel files, make quick edits, read documents, and write short notes or reports without leaving the environment.

Not an Office Workstation

The TRE is mostly oriented for analysis, rather than office work.

For data processing, repeatable analysis, and large or complex datasets, use Python or Jupyter notebooks. LibreOffice is best for quick inspection and light editing.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: The platform provides LibreOffice 26.8.1 (64-bit), installed for all users. No administrator rights are needed to use it.

docs.title: Offline Operation
docs.text: Glasgow TRE has no internet access. Update checks, online help, and telemetry are switched off.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
You can start LibreOffice in either of these ways:

  • Double-click the LibreOffice shortcut on your desktop.
  • Open the Start Menu and select LibreOffice.

You can also open a file directly: right-click it in File Explorer, choose Open with, and select the LibreOffice application you want.

Save Work to Your Project Drive

Always save research files to your project drive (V:\<project-name>\). Local drives are not backed up, and files saved there may be lost.

docs.title: How-To Guides
docs.text: Beyond the basic usage of LibreOffice, you can use it to convert files to other formats, such as PDF or CSV. The following are some common tasks that may be useful.

1. Open the document.
  2. Choose File → Export as → Export as PDF….
  3. Select your options, click Export, and save to your project folder on V:\.

Check Before Exporting Results

Files that leave the TRE must go through the approved export process. See Data Transfer Guidelines.

docs.title: Convert files from the command line
docs.text:
For many files at once, use the command line. Open PowerShell and run LibreOffice in headless mode with soffice.com:

# Convert a Word document to PDF
& "C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\program\soffice.com" --headless --convert-to pdf "V:\my-project\reports\summary.docx" --outdir "V:\my-project\reports"

# Convert an Excel spreadsheet to CSV
& "C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\program\soffice.com" --headless --convert-to csv "V:\my-project\data\tables.xlsx" --outdir "V:\my-project\data"
Flag Purpose --headless Runs without opening a window. --convert-to <format> Target format, for example pdf, csv, docx, or xlsx. --outdir <directory> Folder where the converted file is saved.

Use soffice.com, Not soffice.exe

The .com version prints output in your terminal. Always put file paths in double quotes and do not end a path with a backslash (use "V:\my-project", not "V:\my-project\").

docs.title: Settings and Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Your settings roam with you: preferences, dictionaries, and templates are saved in your user profile and follow you between workstations.
  • Document recovery: if LibreOffice closes unexpectedly, reopen it and choose Recover when prompted.
  • Large files: Calc is not designed for very large datasets. If a file is slow to open or exceeds the sheet row limit (about 1 million rows), use Python instead.
  • Need help or a missing feature? Contact the helpdesk at tre@glasgow.com.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text: Glasgow TRE allow Python development is based on a Python Management approach, which allows user to tailor their their Python environments according to their specific needs.

docs.title: Management
docs.text: This is based on Astral's uv Python manager. Users can install, manage, and switch between multiple Python versions and their associated packages.

docs.title: Python Builds
docs.text:
Selected Python builds are sourced from astral-sh/python-build-standalone and hosted in an internal mirror. uv then is then downloading the selected version according to your request.

Supported Python Versions

please refer to the Available Python Releases section for a list of available versions.

docs.title: Available Packages
docs.text: Python package managers are preconfigured configured to use our internal PyPA mirror. This includes pip and uv.

docs.title: IDE Support
docs.text:
Environments made with uv are fully compatible with modern IDEs such as VS Code. This creates an ideal enviroment for developers who want to write and test their Python code.

Note

Jupyter notebooks use the same underlying infrastructure but are pre-configured and ready to be used.

docs.title: Additional Python Packages
docs.text:
If you need additional packages, please submit a package request ticket through your Glasgow TRE representative or send an email to the helpdesk at tre@glasgow.com.

After we review your request, the packages will be made available to all users and projects.

Information Needed

Make sure to include the library name, requested version, and analytical rationale.

Capabilities Enabled:

  • Released 408 package versions (315 new packages, 70 version updates) to the Glasgow TRE production PyPI mirror.
  • Deep Learning & LLM Foundation Ecosystem: PyTorch suite (torch, torchvision, torchaudio, torchmetrics, pytorch-lightning, lightning), TensorFlow & Keras (tensorflow, keras, flwr), Hugging Face & LLM tooling (transformers, tokenizers, datasets, peft, sentence-transformers, sentencepiece, tiktoken, vllm, outlines-core, compressed-tensors, gguf, anthropic, openai, mistral-common).
  • Distributed Computing & Workflow Orchestration: Scalable multi-node execution and pipeline management with Ray (ray), Dask (dask, distributed), PySpark (pyspark), Snakemake (snakemake), and Prefect (prefect).
  • Spatial Omics & Multi-dimensional Biomedical Imaging: Multi-scale spatial omics, imaging, and single-cell analysis (napari and GUI ecosystem, monai, spatialdata, spatialdata-plot, squidpy, mudata, muon, ome-zarr, pims, cyvcf2, pysam, hail).
  • Geospatial Analytics & High-Performance Visualization: Spatial geometry analysis and large-scale raster rendering (geopandas, shapely, pyproj, pyogrio, datashader, vispy, colorcet, xarray-spatial).
  • Advanced Machine Learning, Model Explainability & Responsible AI: Gradient boosting frameworks (xgboost, lightgbm, catboost), imbalance handling (imbalanced-learn), interpretability (lime, captum), model monitoring (evidently), and differential privacy/PII governance (diffprivlib, opacus, presidio-analyzer, pysyft).
  • Cloud Object Storage & Enterprise SDKs: Cloud connectors and high-throughput transfer libraries for Azure (azure-identity, azure-storage-blob, azure-mgmt-storage), AWS S3 (boto3, botocore, s3fs, s3transfer), and Redis (redis, burner-redis).
  • GPU Runtimes, Accelerated Kernels & Modern Services: NVIDIA CUDA 12 ecosystem runtime libraries (nvidia-*-cu12, cupy-cuda12x), CUDA 13 CUTLASS, accelerated inference kernels (flashinfer-python, xgrammar), Model Context Protocol (mcp), gRPC (grpcio), high-performance web frameworks (fastapi-cli, litestar, websockets, uvloop), and modern data modeling (sqlmodel).
